title: Notes for a Community Exhibition
paragraphs: The community center was planning an exhibition about everyday experiences. Students volunteered to select the written material. Their challenge was to find a balance between vivid individual moments and a larger theme that visitors could follow without already knowing the people involved.

Several records provided a starting point for the discussion. The protester chose to defy the order and remain in the square. A strong lock may deter thieves from entering the shed. The researchers dispute the finding because the measurements appear incorrect. The strongest team continued to dominate the competition.

Other records complicated that first impression and encouraged a closer reading. The hikers had to endure freezing temperatures until rescuers arrived. Thick mud can hinder progress along the trail. A neutral teacher will mediate the disagreement between the two students. All cyclists must obey the traffic signals.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?

to discourage an action through fear of consequences
to challenge the truth or correctness of
to have control or power over
